# ADR-079: Mobile App-Shell & POS Mobile Radial FAB

**Status:** ACCEPTED · **AMENDED 2026-04-17 (v2 + v3)**
**Date:** 2026-04-17
**Supersedes/amends:** ADR-070 (Master-Detail Navigation Shell) on mobile
**Related:** ADR-057 (POS Mobile Ordering), ADR-071 (i18n and Theme)
**Tracks:** PR #12 (`5e6412a`), PR #13 (`49baba8`), PR #14 (`a8cc752`), PR #15 (v3 — pending)

## Context

Two UX regressions were surfaced on mobile after ADR-070 shipped:

1. **Global chrome clipped content on `/pos/mobile`.** The bottom-sheet `CartDrawer` and the app-shell `BottomNav` (added by PR #12) both anchored to `fixed bottom-0`, overlapping the cart card. The cashier could not reach the checkout button reliably.
2. **Primary controls were hard to reach with one hand.** The redesigned `Topbar` (compact, ≤`h-14`) still hosted a bell icon, a standalone theme toggle, and a language switcher — on a narrow mobile viewport this competes with the tenant brand + module tabs and forces horizontal scroll. POS Mobile additionally had a sticky in-page `Header` that duplicated the module chrome.

The app also lacks a true mobile-native navigation pattern. ADR-070 assumes desktop, where the master Topbar hosts horizontal module tabs that do not scale below 768px.

## Decision

Introduce an explicit **mobile app-shell** composed of three pieces, and carve out `/pos/mobile` as a **fullscreen canvas** without global chrome.

### 1. Compact Topbar + user-avatar Dropdown
- Remove the standalone notification bell; render unread count as a **red badge on the user avatar** (value from `GET /api/notifications/count`, polled every 60 s by `useNotificationCount`).
- Consolidate **Theme toggle**, **Settings**, **Sign out** into the user avatar `Dropdown` (new reusable primitive at `components/ui/Dropdown.jsx`).
- Sidebar footer no longer duplicates Settings/Sign out.
- Module tabs remain horizontal but are hidden on mobile (replaced by `BottomNav`).

### 2. BottomNav for mobile primary navigation
- 5 tabs: **Overview · Inbox · POS · Marketing Brief · CRM** (the core operational loops of a Thai F&B SME).
- Per-tab unread badges sourced from `useNotificationCount`'s `breakdown` (inbox ← open conversations, POS ← pending orders).
- Secondary modules (Kitchen, Schedule, Courses, Employees, Tasks, Help, UAT) remain reachable via the hamburger drawer — the existing `Sidebar` mounted in `mobileOpen` mode.
- `safe-area-inset-bottom` padding for iOS home indicator.
- Hidden on fullscreen routes (see §3).

### 3. `/pos/mobile` as a fullscreen canvas
- Both `Topbar` and `BottomNav` early-return `null` when `pathname === '/pos/mobile'`.
- The in-page sticky `Header` (back / POS Mobile title / cashier / badges) is removed entirely.
- **Cart** is a **right-side slide-out drawer** (`CartDrawer`) toggled by a floating cart FAB (top-right) carrying the item-count badge. Auto-opens the first time an item is added; backdrop tap closes.
- **Secondary actions** live in a **Radial/Arc FAB** (`RadialMenu`, bottom-right). Tapping the plus icon fans satellites in a quarter-arc; active state tints orange. Satellites currently:
  - Member · Table (ONSITE only) · Guest Count (ONSITE only) · Reset Cart (when cart has items) · Exit POS.
- Order Type Selector remains visible at the top (most important cashier decision).

### 4. Notification count API
- `GET /api/notifications/count` — aggregates `Conversation.status='open'` + `Order.status='PENDING'` + `Task.status='PENDING'` into `{ count, breakdown }`. No new Prisma model; guarded by `withAuth({ domain: 'dashboard', action: 'R' })`.
- Client hook: `useNotificationCount` — 60 s poll + refetch on visibility.

## Rationale

- **Thumb-friendly:** Primary actions now live at screen edges — BottomNav at the bottom (reachable), avatar badge + cart FAB at the top corners, radial FAB at the bottom-right for POS Mobile's cashier actions.
- **Familiarity for Thai SME users:** LINE, Shopee, Grab, Lineman all use bottom tab navigation on mobile — matching reduces onboarding friction.
- **No architectural coupling:** The radial FAB and BottomNav are additive components; removing the app-shell chrome on `/pos/mobile` is a localised opt-out guarded by `pathname` — other routes are unaffected.
- **Works around single-operator tenants:** A solo owner running register duty needs both hands free; the radial FAB surfaces member/table/guest entry without a modal stack.

## Impact

- **New components:** `components/ui/Dropdown.jsx`, `components/layouts/BottomNav.jsx`, `components/pos/mobile/RadialMenu.jsx`.
- **Rewritten:** `components/pos/mobile/CartDrawer.jsx` (bottom sheet → right-side drawer).
- **Edited:** `components/layouts/Topbar.jsx`, `components/layouts/Sidebar.jsx`, `app/(dashboard)/layout.jsx`, `app/(dashboard)/pos/mobile/page.jsx`.
- **New API:** `app/api/notifications/count/route.js` + `hooks/useNotificationCount.js`.
- **ADR-070** stays accepted for the desktop shell but this ADR supersedes it for mobile.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep bottom-sheet Cart, raise its z-index above BottomNav.** Rejected — still clips the product grid (the real fix is fewer stacked bottom-anchored elements).
- **Move secondary POS actions into a traditional drawer from the left.** Rejected — conflicts with the hamburger drawer used for app navigation and requires two-hand operation.
- **Inline notifications list under the avatar.** Deferred — count-only badge is enough for v1; a full notification centre is a follow-up.
- **Separate `/pos/mobile` into its own route group outside `(dashboard)`.** Rejected as premature — the `pathname` opt-out is one line per component and keeps the cashier inside the same auth/tenant providers.

## Follow-ups

- Hoist `@keyframes fade-in` / `.animate-fade-in` into `src/styles/globals.css` (currently redefined per-page).
- Consider switching the 60 s poll to Pusher push when a notifications table lands.
- Mobile landscape tablet (≥ 768 px viewport flipped) currently uses the desktop shell; validate with a real device before shipping to production.
- Add Cypress/Playwright coverage for `/pos/mobile` cart + radial FAB flows.

## Amendment v2 (2026-04-17, PR #14)

Boss feedback after PRs #12 and #13: keep the BottomNav, but **collapse the mobile Topbar entirely into the BottomNav** so every piece of mobile chrome lives in one place; let the Radial FAB stand in for the Sidebar on mobile.

### Changes
1. **Topbar is hidden below `md`.** Wrapper receives `hidden md:block`. Desktop unchanged.
2. **BottomNav grows from 5 → 6 items:** `Home · Inbox · POS · Brief · More · Profile`.
   - **More** opens a bottom sheet with CRM + secondary modules (Kitchen, Schedule, Courses, Employees, Tasks, Help, UAT). CRM moved out of the primary row per Boss's choice (option "C").
   - **Profile** opens a bottom sheet — full tenant header (logo + shop name + user name + email + role) + Dark/Light toggle + TH/EN switcher + Settings + Sign out.
   - Per-tab badges remain split: Inbox ← `openConversations`, POS ← `pendingOrders`. Profile avatar carries `pendingTasks` so no signal is orphaned.
3. **Radial FAB becomes contextual** instead of static.
   - Satellites are derived from `modules[currentKey].subFeatures` (max 5).
   - On `/inbox`: ทั้งหมด · Facebook · LINE · รอตอบ. On `/pos`: POS Mobile · จัดการโต๊ะ · Seating Monitor. Etc.
   - Links go through `RadialMenu`'s new `href` support (renders `<Link>` satellites).
   - Hidden on desktop (`hideOnDesktop`) and lifted above the BottomNav (`aboveBottomNav`).
4. **Sidebar drawer is effectively retired on mobile** — there is no longer a hamburger to open it. The component remains mounted for desktop hover-expand; the mobileOpen state is unreachable on mobile but harmless.

### Rationale
- One chrome element on mobile reduces vertical space wasted on navigation; the product grid / inbox list reclaims the top of the viewport.
- Consolidating user controls (theme, language, settings, sign out, secondary modules) into the Profile sheet keeps them one tap away without competing with primary navigation.
- A contextual Radial FAB is more useful than the previous static POS-only satellites: it replaces the old contextual Sidebar on every mobile page.

### Impact
- `components/layouts/BottomNav.jsx` — rewritten (6 items + embedded Profile/More bottom sheets).
- `components/layouts/Topbar.jsx` — adds `hidden md:block` wrapper class; no logic change.
- `components/pos/mobile/RadialMenu.jsx` — supports `href` actions, `hideOnDesktop`, and `aboveBottomNav` props.
- `app/(dashboard)/layout.jsx` — mounts a mobile-only contextual RadialMenu driven by `modules[currentKey].subFeatures`.
- `/pos/mobile` untouched — still owns a dedicated RadialMenu (member/table/guest/reset/back) and its own CartDrawer.

## Amendment v3 (2026-04-17, PR #15)

Boss observed that the global **AI Chat Bot FAB** (`.ai-fab`, `AiFab.jsx`) still lives at `bottom: 2rem; right: 2rem` and collides with the mobile contextual Radial FAB added in v2. Fix: **move the chat bot into the BottomNav as a centre combo button**.

### Changes
1. **BottomNav: 6 → 7 items.** Layout is now:
   ```
   Home · Inbox · POS · [Combo] · Brief · More · Profile
   ```
   The 4th cell hosts a circular **combo FAB** with a horizontally split icon:
   - **Top half** — `Plus` (orange gradient) → Radial (module sub-features).
   - **Bottom half** — `Bot` (indigo gradient) → AI Chat bot.

2. **Combo gestures** (Pointer Events, `touch-action: none`):
   - **Tap** (`dt < 400 ms`, `|dy| < 12 px`) → open **Radial** (default action).
   - **Drag up** (`dy < -24 px`) → open **Radial** (explicit).
   - **Drag down** (`dy > +24 px`) → open **Chat**.
   - During drag the active half tints a lighter shade + a small ▲/▼ cue appears beside the button.

3. **RadialMenu** gains three props:
   - `open` / `onOpenChange` — controlled open state.
   - `hideTrigger` — suppresses the internal trigger button (the combo button above is the trigger now).
   - `anchor: 'bc'` (bottom-centre) — satellites fan in a symmetric ~140° arc around straight-up, matching the combo button's centre position.

4. **`AiFab` hidden on mobile.** CSS-only: `@media (max-width: 767px) { .ai-fab { display: none; } }` in `AiAssistant.css`. Desktop unchanged.

5. **`AiChatPopup` becomes a responsive bottom sheet on mobile.** Mobile CSS docks it to the top of the BottomNav (`bottom: calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`) with full width and a top-rounded sheet shape.

6. **`(dashboard)/layout.jsx`** no longer mounts the contextual RadialMenu — ownership moved inside `BottomNav`, which holds the radial + chat state and renders both from a single tree so the combo button can drive them.

### Rationale
- **No more FAB overlap.** The only elements anchored bottom-right on mobile are the BottomNav (fixed) and, on `/pos/mobile`, its own dedicated Radial (which still works because BottomNav isn't rendered there).
- **Single-glance discoverability.** The half-split icon literally tells the user there are two destinations; the tiny ▲/▼ cue during drag reinforces direction.
- **One container owns the state.** Having BottomNav own both the radial and the chat avoids cross-component event wiring and prop-drilling.

### Impact
- `components/layouts/BottomNav.jsx` — rewritten (7 items + combo button + pointer-gesture handlers; mounts contextual `RadialMenu` and `AiChatPopup`).
- `components/pos/mobile/RadialMenu.jsx` — adds `open`/`onOpenChange`/`hideTrigger` and the `bc` anchor.
- `components/ai/AiAssistant.css` — `.ai-fab` hidden below `md`; `.ai-chat-popup` becomes a mobile sheet.
- `app/(dashboard)/layout.jsx` — removes the mobile RadialMenu mount (BottomNav owns it).
- `/pos/mobile` still owns its own RadialMenu (member/table/guest/reset/back) and CartDrawer — untouched.

### Alternatives Considered
- **Move the `.ai-fab` to bottom-left on mobile.** Rejected — still shares real estate with the main content and requires a second discoverable floating control.
- **Tap top half = Radial, Tap bottom half = Chat (no drag).** Rejected as more fragile on small buttons; drag gesture with tap-as-default is more forgiving.
- **Double-tap to switch modes.** Rejected — drag is a more natural direction metaphor and doesn't conflict with the tap-to-default path.

### Follow-ups
- Add haptic feedback (`navigator.vibrate(10)`) on successful drag past threshold — iOS ignores but Android users get a confirmation buzz.
- Consider a tutorial coachmark on first open to explain the split icon.
- If future features demand a 3rd destination, switch the centre to a "long-press = menu" pattern rather than cramming more gestures.
